modern: If a man is mistaken, teach him kindly and show him his error. But if you are not able to, blame yourself, or do not blame even yourself.
original: If a man is mistaken, instruct him kindly and show him his error. But if thou art not able, blame thyself, or blame not even thyself.

explained.summary: When someone gets something wrong, correct them kindly and show them where they went astray. If you can’t get through to them, look first at how you went about it and blame yourself. Or better still, don’t blame anyone at all, not even yourself, and let it go.
explained.today: Think of explaining something to a relative who has shared a dubious article, or to a new colleague who keeps making the same mistake. Patience works better than scorn, and if it doesn’t land, try a different approach instead of writing them off.
